# Vendor

The Vendors module in CorpCash enables administrators to manage and maintain the organization's vendor records from a centralized interface. The module is intended to provide administrators with a consolidated view of vendors associated with the organization and support vendor-related administrative activities within the CorpCash platform.

<figure><img src="../../../.gitbook/assets/image (156).png" alt=""><figcaption></figcaption></figure>

Administrators can use the Vendors module to access vendor information, review existing vendor records, search for a specific vendor, and perform the actions made available according to their assigned permissions. The module provides a centralized location for maintaining vendor information and helps administrators efficiently manage vendor-related activities.

#### Accessing the Vendors Module

The Vendors option is available below Employees in the main navigation menu. Selecting this option takes the administrator from the employee-management area to the vendor-management interface.

{% stepper %}
{% step %}
### Login to Corpcash

To access the Vendors module, log in to the CorpCash application using valid administrator credentials.

<figure><img src="../../../.gitbook/assets/image.png" alt=""><figcaption></figcaption></figure>
{% endstep %}

{% step %}
### Vendor Module

From the left-side navigation panel, select **Vendors-> Manage**. As soon as the user clicks the system opens the Vendors details page as shown below in the image.

&#x20;![](<../../../.gitbook/assets/image (1).png>)
{% endstep %}

{% step %}
### Vendor Detail

Here the administrator can view the available vendor records and access the vendor-management functionality configured for the organization.

<figure><img src="../../../.gitbook/assets/image (2).png" alt=""><figcaption></figcaption></figure>
{% endstep %}
{% endstepper %}

#### Searching Vendors

<figure><img src="../../../.gitbook/assets/image (3).png" alt=""><figcaption></figcaption></figure>

The Vendors page provides search functionality to help administrators locate a specific vendor from the available vendor records. Search functionality is particularly useful when the organization maintains a large number of vendor records. Once the required vendor is identified, the administrator can open the vendor record using the “view” button action provided against the corresponding record.
